title: Pre-Analysis — Interim Shaft Seal Kit for the Green System Engine Driven Pump
abstract: Short pre-analysis of an interim seal kit raised to hold the shaft leak rate down while a full case drain redesign was scoped, focused on what the kit does to the published removal, installation and fault-isolation content.

sections.objective: Confirm that an interim seal kit can be released quickly against the recurring green system fluid loss without prejudicing the architectural change already being scoped behind it. The pre-analysis was deliberately narrow: no attempt was made to assess the architecture, only to establish that the kit is reversible, that it does not change the pump interface, and that the published content can describe an aircraft carrying it without a second procedure for every task.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and all three are documentation rather than design. The pump removal task names the seal assembly the kit replaces, and because the kit is fitted at shop level rather than on wing the task needs to say so explicitly or a line technician will attempt it at the aircraft. The installation task calls a torque value that the kit's revised retainer changes, and the value is quoted rather than referenced, so it has to be corrected in place. The fault-isolation procedure for fluid found in the accessory gearbox area uses a leak rate threshold set for the original seal; on a kit aircraft that threshold is met long before the seal is actually failing and the pump would be removed unnecessarily. Nothing was found that would constrain the architectural change that follows.
sections.next_steps: Publish the three manual corrections in the same revision batch as the kit bulletin, and mark the removal task explicitly as a shop level activity. Record in the dossier that the kit is interim and reversible so that the architectural change behind it is not asked to accommodate it. Review the leak rate threshold again when the architectural change is released, because it will move a second time.

similarity_seeds: shaft seal kit against recurring hydraulic fluid loss
leak rate threshold in a hydraulic fault isolation procedure

tasks.title: Sweep pump removal and installation content for affected values
Check the fault-isolation leak rate threshold against the kit

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task names the seal assembly the kit replaces and does not say at what level the work is done. The kit is a shop level fit, and the task as written invites a line attempt at the aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Name both seal assemblies and state the shop level restriction in the task.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task quotes a retainer torque value rather than referencing it. The kit changes the retainer, so the quoted value is wrong on a kit pump and there is no reference to follow instead.
expected_findings.resolution: Correct the value in place and add the kit condition beside it.

expected_findings.rationale: The leak rate threshold in the fault-isolation procedure was set for the original seal. On a kit pump it is met well before the seal is failing, so the procedure removes serviceable pumps.
expected_findings.resolution: Revise the threshold and publish it in the same batch as the kit bulletin.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position subject to the three manual corrections travelling with the kit bulletin. The kit is recorded as interim and reversible so that the architectural change behind it is unconstrained.
